title: I Hear the Sunspot: Limit
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: In this continuation of I Hear the Sunspot, Kohei, a university student with a hearing disability, and Taichi, who has entered the working world, begin a life together as a couple. The volumes follow deaf and hard-of-hearing characters at work and study, including a coworker struggling to be included at a company retreat and a debate over interpreters, implants and surgery.
life_message: A good life comes from being understood and understanding others, with independence and support held in balance.

folkways.japan: The company retreat and pressure to fit in at work reflect Japanese workplace group norms, which the deaf characters must navigate; described not judged.

delivery.evidence: The Outerhaven describes gradual 'slow burn' growth and varied deaf perspectives, not moralizing.

personified.ideology: a full life without hearing; rejection of implants

delivery.note: Different deaf characters hold conflicting views on interpreters and implants, and the reviewer finds each given a fair hearing.

winners_losers: No single view wins: inclusion, self-advocacy and the couple's mutual support are all shown as part of a good life, and conflicting deaf perspectives are respected.
